subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit account-scoped bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but fallback routing controls agent workspace, tools, model/provider context, and session state, and repository policy treats fallback behavior plus provider/session routing as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add warning or doctor/status guidance when Discord accounts appear intended for same-named agents without bindings.

options.title: Repair source PR first
options.body: Use the prior/fork PR only as source material after resolving conflicts, adding configured-agent guards, and proving real Discord behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal on shared routing, Discord route-resolution, and routing docs.
